title: US Treasury yields continue to break higher - is 6% now in play?
description: The selloff in the bond market isn't showing much sign of letting up. 10-year Treasury yields have pushed up to 5.18%, extending the breakout above 5% and putting another important technical area firmly into view. The next major hurdle on the chart sits around the 5.25% to 5.30% region, roughly where yields topped out during 2006-07. So, what's next from here? Well, if the 2006-07 highs give way, I reckon the conversation around 6% Treasury yields will then start becoming a lot less theoretical. title: Trump-Xi summit extends the trade truce but leaves the biggest market questions unresolved
description: And so the Trump-Xi summit this week delivered what markets probably needed most. That being no fresh escalation between the two largest economies in the world. But beyond that, there wasn't much of any breakthrough either. The clearest takeaway is the extension of the existing US-China trade truce by another two months to 10 January. That keeps the existing tariffs regime in place and gives both sides more time to negotiate what Bessent has described as a potentially broader agreement. title: German consumer climate darkens ahead of October as higher energy costs bite
description: Germany October GfK consumer climate -30.6 vs -27.4 expected Prior -26.6; revised to -26.8 The breakdownThat is a notable miss on estimates as German consumer sentiment weakens more sharply than expected heading into October. The main culprit is rising energy prices and that is weighing on purchasing power of households especially. title: Spain Q2 GDP confirmed at 0.7% as domestic demand keeps growth resilient
description: Spain Q2 final GDP +0.7% vs +0.7% q/q expected Prior +0.6% The breakdownThe final estimate confirms that the Spanish economy grew by 0.7% in the second quarter, accelerating slightly from 0.6% growth in Q1. Domestic demand remains the main engine of the economy, contributing 1.1% to quarterly GDP growth. By aggregate demand, household consumption increased by 1.2% and government consumption by 0.5%.
